mainEntity.name: How do you calculate a product price?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start from landed cost, then apply one rule. For a target margin, divide the cost by one minus the margin: a $22.00 case at 28% prices at $30.56.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between markup and margin?

acceptedAnswer.text: Markup is a percentage of your cost, margin is a percentage of the price. A 28% markup on a $22.00 case gives $28.16, while a 28% margin needs $30.56, a $2.40 gap.

mainEntity.name: What is a good margin on a case of food?

acceptedAnswer.text: It varies by category, so compare against your own blend rather than a benchmark. Staples run thin and specialty runs wide, and the mix is what pays the overhead.

mainEntity.name: Should you price off a flat profit per case?

acceptedAnswer.text: Only on a narrow catalog. A flat $8.00 gives 26.7% on a $22.00 case, but the same $8.00 on a cheaper case is a much fatter margin and on a dearer one it is far too thin.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth matching a competitor's price?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check the margin before you match. At $31.00 against a $22.00 case the match leaves 29.0%, which beats both other rules here. That will not hold if your cost is higher than theirs.

mainEntity.name: What costs belong in the price of a case?

acceptedAnswer.text: Product cost, inbound freight, handling, and the shrink you expect on that item. Leave any of them out and the margin on screen is not the margin you bank.
